preamble:
As data science rapidly advances, fueled by recent developments in generative artificial intelligence (AI), it is crucial for Statistics Canada, as a National Statistical Organization, to remain at the forefront of these changes. The increasing importance of AI has transformed the field of data and digital, necessitating new and enhanced skill sets for the workforce. This revised competency profile addresses these developments, ensuring that our workforce possesses the essential tools to excel within the budding domain of data science and AI.

Acknowledgements: This document was adapted from its previous version published in 2022, Competency Profiles to Shape Data Science in the Public Service and the Government of Canada Data Competency Framework and was informed by input from a multidisciplinary working group.

The competencies are divided into two categories: (1) Behavioural Skills and (2) Technical Skills. Each competency describes four levels of proficiency which build upon one another: Foundational, Intermediate, Advanced and Lead. A general outline of the depth of knowledge and expertise required per level of proficiency follows.

Foundational: Demonstrated ability to consistently deliver tasks of low complexity under minimal supervision and tasks of moderate complexity under strong supervision or with direct mentoring. Usually associated with junior or entry-level roles.

Intermediate: Demonstrated ability to consistently deliver tasks of low to moderate complexity under minimal supervision and tasks of higher-level complexity under moderate supervision and mentoring. Usually associated with Intermediate roles.

Advanced: Demonstrated ability to scope, undertake, and deliver tasks of moderate to high complexity under minimal levels of supervision. Demonstrated ability to mentor others in lower levels of skill development, either through direct supervision or by setting examples and providing explanations. Usually associated with senior technical advisor or entry-level supervisory roles.

Lead: Demonstrated ability to identify, scope, undertake, and deliver tasks of significant complexity with wide areas of impact, even in challenging circumstances. Demonstrated ability to Lead the development of tasks, and potentially teams, for the organization in this area. Usually associated with managerial or technical Lead roles.

This competency profile can be used as a guide by managers to assess data science and artificial intelligence skills by level and to identify specific areas for performance improvement. Employees can consult the details provided in this document to better understand the knowledge and skills that they require to progress within the organization.

This document can be used at a higher level to support succession planning by aiding in the creation of targeted talent development plans to address skills gaps. This profile can also be used to benefit workforce planning by helping human resource teams spot high-potential talent, and to pinpoint critical roles and skills to guide recruitment and development initiatives. On an organizational level, this profile can be used to ensure that an organization's staff is equipped with the knowledge and skills required to achieve their strategic goals and priorities.

This competency profile recognizes that data science and AI are a rapidly evolving field, and it includes anticipated shifts in the tasks for competencies that will likely be impacted. An icon has been inserted below the competencies that may be potentially impacted with potential changes indicated beside it. Insights into the future of work are included to support users of this document in preparing for evolving expectations in the domain.

Overview: Data Science and Artificial Intelligence Functional Community

Data scientists and AI experts use data to identify and resolve complex business issues. Their interdisciplinary approach incorporates techniques and knowledge from various scientific and computer science fields, such as economics, statistics, mathematics, predictive analytics, and machine learning. Typically, they are part of multidisciplinary project teams that include data science engineers, business owners, social scientists, methodologists, business analysts, project managers, and software engineers/designers, among others.

The roles and responsibilities of a data scientist and AI expert may encompass, but are not limited to, those outlined within generic data science job descriptions. Additionally, interdepartmental, and government-wide concepts can be found in the centralized classification repository (PCIS). Consult Appendix A for Statistics Canada's specific data science job families. Consult Appendix B for mapping the competencies to various occupational groups.

Key Roles

Data scientists and AI experts can take on various roles depending on their skills and level of proficiency across different areas of the field. The below chart outlines five key domains, describing the core capabilities, levels of proficiency along with potential job titles to provide an overview of the primary roles these experts may take on at Statistics Canada.

Learner personas help to humanize the target audience, clarify their goals and barriers, and guide the design of competency-based learning experiences. By capturing key characteristics, these personas support the development of more relevant, accessible, and personalized upskilling pathways. Their inclusion ensures the framework remains learner-centred and adaptable to real-world needs. Please note that this competency profile and the persona descriptions provided below are not exhaustive; rather, they serve as a guide for the baseline requirements for these roles, as it pertains to performance management.

behavioural_competencies.name: Thinking Things Through (Create Vision and Strategy)
behavioural_competencies.description: Thinking Things Through is the ability to systematically analyze problems, identify patterns and connections, and develop well-informed plans and recommendations. This competency involves asking the right questions, evaluating cause and effect relationships, and turning analysis into clear strategies that align with organizational goals.
behavioural_competencies.why_this_competency_matters: The ability to think things through forms the backbone of effective decision-making and strategic planning within data science and across organizations. Individuals skilled in this competency turn complex analytical issues into clear, actionable strategies, ensuring recommendations are both relevant and impactful. Mastery of this area enables data scientists and Leaders to respond decisively to evolving priorities, align team activities with business objectives, and guide organizations toward innovative solutions that drive long-term success.

Foundational: Ask the right questions to identify relevant problems/issues.
Frame questions explicitly for data to inform answers.
Consult with appropriate authorities to identify what constitutes high-quality evidence.
Recognize connections and develop short-term plans and recommendations.
Use cause and effect relationships to analyze problems systematically.
Resolve problems in a sound, logical and decisive manner.
Intermediate: Respond to complex analytical issues.
Develop short- and long-term plans and recommendations.
Use cause and effect relationships to analyze problems, interpret information, and develop recommendations.
Advanced: Analyze complex problems by identifying patterns, connections, and implications to inform short- and long-term recommendations for management, clients, and stakeholders.
Evaluate and compare diverse information sources to resolve issues logically and decisively.
Apply contextual understanding of the organizational environment to guide sound analysis and decision-making.
Collaborate effectively to implement concrete actions aligned with evolving priorities.
Coordinate team efforts to support the development and execution of organizational strategies and objectives.
Communicate with clarity and conviction to ensure shared understanding and alignment.
Lead: Inform analysis with a thorough understanding of the environment.
Translate implementation strategies, objectives and direction into concrete activities.
Contribute expertise and insight to the development and implementation of organizational strategies.
Communicate with clarity and conviction.
Respond to changes in direction and organizational priorities.
Design and implement solutions to operational challenges.

behavioural_competencies.name: Showing Initiative and Being Action Oriented (Achieve Results; Promote Innovation and Guide Change)
behavioural_competencies.description: Showing Initiative and Being Action Oriented is the ability to proactively accomplish tasks, adapt to shifting priorities, and effectively plan to achieve results even when faced with challenges. It includes anticipating and overcoming obstacles, driving projects forward, and using resourcefulness to both improve performance and promote innovation. This competency extends to encouraging experimentation and new ideas, demonstrating resilience amid change, and taking ownership for outcomes.
behavioural_competencies.why_this_competency_matters: Consistently delivering results and embracing innovation are critical in fast-evolving fields like data science. Individuals who show initiative drive progress, help their teams adapt quickly, and foster a culture of creative problem-solving. This competency enables organizations to respond to change, seize new opportunities, and continuously improve.

Foundational: Accomplish own share of work
Respond to changes in organizational priority, revising own work when conditions change
Plan for contingencies to deal with unforeseen events or setbacks
Break activities into smaller components to facilitate completion
Intermediate: Evaluate project plans to ensure that goals are reached
Contribute to annual plans for the work unit considering a range of factors in the planning process
Advanced: Plan strategically by aligning short- and long-term goals, adjusting actions as priorities evolve
Negotiate timelines and commitments to ensure delivery against objectives
Establish and apply objective metrics to evaluate performance and drive improvement
Apply risk management strategies to anticipate and mitigate potential impacts
Identify and remove barriers to innovation while promoting creative solutions
Encourage diverse thinking and experimentation to foster innovation
Adapt based on lessons learned, demonstrating resilience and agility
Coordinate and prioritize work to optimize resources and achieve results
Monitor and revise plans using data, evidence, and contextual insight
Demonstrate accountability and stewardship in decision-making and resource use
Lead: Align people with work to achieve organizational objectives and results
Monitor and control work unit resources
Set and revise operational plans to reflect changing priorities or conditions
Inform decision-making with sound understanding of context, data and evidence
Demonstrate and promote stewardship of financial and organizational resources
Make challenging decisions and take action at the opportune time
Take ownership and acknowledge impact and outcome of decisions
Encourage and apply sound risk management practices
Identify opportunities for and barriers to innovation
Propose creative practices, concepts or products
Encourage employees to generate new and innovative approaches
Adjust practices to address lessons learned following setbacks and mistakes
Adapt plans in response to changes in direction and priorities
Evaluate the impact of change on employees and take appropriate action
Demonstrate resilience, composure and a positive outlook in an environment of uncertainty and ambiguity

behavioural_competencies.name: Working Effectively with Others (Mobilize People; Collaborate with Partners and Stakeholders)
behavioural_competencies.description: Working Effectively with Others is the ability to build strong, collaborative relationships within and outside the organization. It involves sharing information openly, encouraging diverse viewpoints, and enabling teamwork to solve problems and achieve shared goals. This competency extends to supporting others through change, providing constructive feedback, mobilizing teams around a common purpose, and fostering partnerships that amplify organizational effectiveness.
behavioural_competencies.why_this_competency_matters: Collaboration is essential for tackling complex problems, driving innovation, and ensuring successful project delivery in data science and beyond. Individuals who excel in this competency help create inclusive, high-performing teams and productive partnerships, Leading to better solutions and sustained organizational growth. By fostering open communication and aligning people around clear objectives, they maximize collective impact and support a positive, adaptable work culture.

Foundational: Share relevant information to facilitate collaboration.
Accomplish independent tasks as part of one's own share of the work.
Work with others to clearly define problems and identify suitable solutions.
Suggest methods and means for maximizing the input and involvement of team members.
Facilitate the expression of diverse points of view to enhance teamwork.
Openly share data/findings to support other teams' work.
Intermediate: Assume additional subject matter responsibility to facilitate the achievement of team goals.
Help stakeholders mitigate resistance to change in their environment.
Build successful initiatives to gain support for ideas.
Review the work of others and provide constructive feedback.
Help others build accessibility into data/AI tools/visualizations as per GC Digital Standards.
Advanced: Facilitate inclusive collaboration by encouraging diverse contributions and perspectives across teams and communities.
Coach and challenge others to build capability and confidence in complex decision-making.
Leverage team strengths and differences to achieve shared goals and foster innovation.
Model open communication by actively listening, giving honest feedback, and recognizing contributions.
Set clear expectations, monitor progress, and address performance constructively.
Promote a shared sense of purpose and continuous learning through goal setting and development opportunities.
Implement strategies that strengthen collaboration and support a high-performance culture.
Lead: Create a sense of common purpose and direction in the organization and among colleagues.
Set clear expectations, and monitor and evaluate performance.
Establish learning and development plans and provide opportunities for continuous learning and development.
Give honest feedback, recognize performance and address non-performance.
Engage employees to gather ideas and input to build cohesive teams.
Set challenging goals for self and model dedication and high performance.
Contribute to building a data and AI literate workforce and data-driven culture.
Build and nurture effective and collaborative networks and relationships with communities of practice, colleagues and stakeholders, and develop a shared responsibility toward data/AI.
Seek and leverage opportunities to enhance outcomes through partnerships.
Encourage employees to participate in collaborative initiatives.
Reflect on impact of issues and perspectives of others.
Implement and communicate strategies that enhance collaboration.
Acknowledge the contribution of others in achieving objectives.

behavioural_competencies.name: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect (Upholds Integrity and Respect)
behavioural_competencies.description: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect is the commitment to ethical behavior, transparency, and fairness in all professional actions. This competency involves consistently adhering to organizational values, ethical guidelines, and legal standards especially when handling sensitive data or implementing analytical methods. It encompasses identifying, discussing, and mitigating ethical risks, supporting colleagues in ethical decision-making, and ensuring practices such as privacy protection, bias reduction, and inclusion are upheld throughout all processes.
behavioural_competencies.why_this_competency_matters: Upholding integrity and respect builds trust among team members, stakeholders, and the public, which is essential in data-driven environments. As data and AI become increasingly integral to decision-making, maintaining rigorous ethical standards helps prevent harm, ensures compliance with legal frameworks, and supports fair, unbiased outcomes. Leaders and practitioners who champion these values help create safe, transparent, and inclusive workplaces.

Foundational: Comply with the Values and Ethics Code for the Public Sector in all aspects of data/AI use.
Discuss ethical concerns with appropriate individuals or channels and seek guidance for ethical/privacy issues.
Identify and report ethical concerns when appropriate.
Adhere to the organization's legal, privacy and ethical frameworks (Privacy Act, Policy on Privacy Protection, etc.) and follow disclosure procedures.
Identify and proactively flag privacy/security/accessibility implications.
Consult responsible AI resources.
Consult key policies/procedures on AI for decision-making.
Ensure privacy/security is set at the right permission levels.
Intermediate: Apply legal and ethical standards when using data, methods, and resources.
Promote a respectful, safe, and transparent workplace.
Explain ethical risks of using historical data in models or predictions.
Evaluate data and models for bias and ensure fairness in outcomes and use best practices to mitigate bias/discrimination in AI.
Analyze the pros and cons of using record-level data in analysis.
Support others in evaluating and resolving complex ethical issues.
Use the Algorithmic Impact Assessment (AIA) tool before deploying automated decision-systems.
Use the AIA tool to identify, evaluate and mitigate analytical risks
Use principles for responsible use of AI in government.
Assess source data for bias, representation, validity and accuracy.
Use security-enhancing tools (e.g., anonymization, masking, de-identification, etc.).
Ensure all visuals meet accessibility/digital standards.
Advanced: Design and execute Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs) and Algorithmic Impact Assessments (AIAs) for AI systems or processes.
Use AIA tool to assess/monitor automated decision risks.
Help others determine when/how to use AIA.
Evaluate the ethical, legal, and social implications of AI models before deployment.
Advise teams on mitigating risks such as bias, misinformation, and overreliance on AI-generated content.
Recommend inclusive design strategies that accommodate diverse user needs and reduce systemic bias.
Interpret and translate Treasury Board Secretariat (TBS) directives (e.g., Directive on Automated Decision-Making) into operational practices.
Ensure compliance with the Voluntary Code of Conduct on Generative AI and the FASTER principles
Mentor others in navigating complex ethical dilemmas in AI deployment and data use.
Provide guidance/advice on responsible data/AI tools (e.g., AIA).
Help colleagues apply accessibility and best practices for communication.
Consult authoritative data sources for alignment with data authority/intended use (e.g. Personal Information Bank (PIB) and PIA's, Digital Privacy Playbook, etc.)
Help and encourage colleagues to apply responsible AI guidance (peer-to-peer support via coaching, communities of practice, research publications, etc.)
Identify and remove barriers to data sharing.
Lead: Ensure that standards and safeguards are in place to protect organizational integrity.
Champion the integration of AI governance frameworks, including human-in-the-loop oversight and transparency protocols.
Develop and enforce ethical review protocols for AI projects, ensuring alignment with TBS and StatCan guidelines.
Guide teams in applying fairness review checklists and employment equity principles in AI-supported processes.
Engage stakeholders to ensure inclusive design strategies that accommodate and benefit from differences between groups.
Lead the implementation of Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs) and Algorithmic Impact Assessments (AIAs) for high impact AI.
Design and implement policies/processes for ethical approaches to research/data use.
Promote responsible/ethical use of AI as an organizational norm.
Champion open data/transparency.

technical_competencies.name: Programming
technical_competencies.description: Knowledge and ability to design, define, construct, enhance, support, and maintain software associated with machine learning.
technical_competencies.why_this_competency_matters: Data scientists are skilled in software development fundamentals, including construction, testing, deployment infrastructure, and development methodologies. Proficient in programmatic data management using open-source data science and AI tools, with a strong grasp of diverse data structures such as vectors, matrices, arrays, and data frames. Continuously evolving technical fluency to build scalable, modern digital solutions.

Foundational: Write basic programs that include variables, loops, conditionals, and functions to perform simple data tasks.
Use basic data structures such as lists, arrays, and dictionaries to store and manipulate data.
Recognize and correct common programming errors, such as syntax and logical mistakes.
Manipulate data using built-in functions and libraries (e.g., Python's Pandas or R's dplyr).
Use at least one open-source programming language, typically Python or R, for basic data manipulation and analysis tasks.
Consider use of open source over commercial tools.
Intermediate: Design and implement functions and classes in Python or R, applying object-oriented programming principles.
Use libraries like Pandas, NumPy, or dplyr to perform data manipulation tasks such as cleaning, transforming, and aggregating data.
Write and implement basic unit tests and functions for quality assurance.
Provide drill down functionality in visualizations.
Advanced: Implement and utilize Advanced data structures (e.g., graphs, trees, heaps) to solve complex data problems.
Analyze and optimize code for performance and efficiency, addressing issues such as time complexity and memory usage.
Ability to implement Advanced frameworks and libraries (e.g., Django, Flask, Spark, Hadoop) for data-driven applications and distributed computing.
Apply software engineering best practices, including clean code principles, modularity, and code documentation.
Develop, implement and troubleshoot system workflows and best coding practices.
Lead: Supervise the design of scalable and maintainable software architectures, ensuring they meet business requirements and are efficient at scale.
Provide mentorship and conduct code reviews to ensure high-quality, maintainable, and efficient code within the development team.
Head cross-functional teams to integrate programming solutions into broader data science, machine learning, or business systems.

technical_competencies.name: Data Processing
technical_competencies.description: Data processing refers to the collection, cleaning, transformation, and manipulation of raw data into a format suitable for analysis and decision-making. It involves handling data from various sources, ensuring its quality, and making it ready for statistical analysis or machine learning models.
technical_competencies.why_this_competency_matters: Data processing is the foundation that ensures that raw datasets are transformed into reliable, analysis-ready formats. Skilled in creating clean, consistent, and scalable data pipelines to power predictive models, business insights, and fast, informed decision-making.

Foundational: Load datasets from common formats (CSV, Excel, SQL) and perform basic cleaning tasks such as handling missing values and formatting issues.
Apply data transformations such as filtering, aggregating, and sorting to prepare data for analysis.
Derive variables to enhance data analysis.
Apply methods to handle missing data (e.g., drop missing records).
Describe the stages of the full data lifecycle (plan, collect, process, use, share, dispose).
Intermediate: Combine multiple datasets from different sources using joins or merges based on common keys, handling inconsistencies in data structure.
Write scripts to automate common data cleaning tasks, such as removing duplicates, correcting data types, and normalizing values.
Process both structured data (e.g., databases, spreadsheets) and unstructured data (e.g., text, logs) for analysis.
Perform complex data manipulations and transformations (e.g., data aggregation, time series processing).
Specify needs regarding tools and infrastructure requirements (e.g., compute capacity).
Create and maintain structured metadata; cleaning and manipulating structured metadata.
Publish data in machine-readable format.
Review and analyze outliers and their role as a potential root cause for quality issues.
Retain/maintain original data for outcome comparison.
Prioritize high-value datasets for interoperability.
Provide transparent documentation and rationale for dataset fitness for use.
Apply agentic AI tools (e.g., LLMs, workflow orchestrators) to automate data ingestion, cleaning, and transformation.
Advanced: Plan, develop, and monitor data processing steps to ensure outputs meet requirements.
Design and optimize end-to-end data pipelines that extract, transform, and load (ETL) large datasets efficiently.
Implement solutions for processing large-scale datasets using tools like Apache Spark or Hadoop, ensuring scalability and performance.
Creating highly structured metadata for granular searches.
Maintain data lineage/audit trails.
Design for access at source (master/reference data).
Build automation/CI pipelines for data/AI lifecycle.
Design architecture/infrastructure that is simple to use, interoperable, and secure.
Evaluate storage options for organizational/industry standards.
Build real-time data pipelines optimised for agentic workflows (e.g., context-aware data retrieval, streaming ingestion).
Lead: Identify and scope significant data processing projects that involve large, complex datasets or novel processing approaches, ensuring alignment with organizational goals.
Oversee the development and implementation of large-scale data processing workflows, Leading teams to automate and scale operations efficiently.
Take responsibility for establishing and enforcing organizational data governance practices, ensuring data quality, integrity, and compliance across business units.
Guide and influence high-level decision-making related to data processing strategies, providing recommendations for improvements and innovations in business processes.
Develop policies/processes for accessibility, collection, interoperability of AI/data.

technical_competencies.name: Mathematics and Statistics
technical_competencies.description: Knowledge in a range of mathematical and statistical techniques, understanding and being able to apply them, and comprehending their underlying assumptions and limitations.
technical_competencies.why_this_competency_matters: Data Science Analysts must have a strong foundation in algebra and probability, with the ability to apply these concepts throughout the data analysis pipeline. Proficient in matrix operations, functional analysis, and equivalence relations. Skilled in statistical theory, particularly analysis of variance and factor analysis, including assumptions and their implications. Capable of interpreting complex statistical output and selecting the most appropriate methods for specific analytical challenges.

Foundational: Understand and apply fundamental statistical concepts such as measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode), variance, and standard deviation.
Ability to summarize and describe the main features of a dataset using visualizations (e.g., histograms, box plots) and numerical summaries (e.g., mean, range).
Understand basic probability concepts, including independent and dependent events, and apply basic probability distributions (e.g., normal distribution).
Familiarity with summarizing data and presenting findings using basic charts and statistics.
Intermediate: Apply inferential statistics such as hypothesis testing (t-tests, chi-square tests), confidence intervals, and p-values to draw conclusions from sample data.
Perform and interpret simple linear regression, including understanding the relationship between dependent and independent variables.
Apply techniques for uncovering patterns in data through visualizations and basic statistical analysis, including correlation and scatter plots.
Perform basic multivariate statistical techniques, such as multiple linear regression or principal component analysis (PCA), to handle multiple variables.
Understand the pros and cons of various statistical tests and when they should be applied.
Advanced: Apply Advanced statistical techniques, such as generalized linear models (GLMs), survival analysis, Bayesian statistics, and time series analysis.
Use Advanced techniques for model evaluation, including cross-validation, performance metrics (e.g., R-squared, AUC), and overfitting prevention.
Implement and interpret more complex models, such as decision trees, random forests, and clustering algorithms.
Write and present detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms using common terminology.
Apply rigorous statistical techniques to solve complex problems.
Provide expert consultation and articulate implications to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Evaluate and compare methodologies to determine the most appropriate approach.
Lead: Spearhead and drive the application of statistical methods to business strategy, ensuring that data science solutions align with organizational goals.
Develop and implement new statistical methods or frameworks to address emerging business challenges.
Guide the creation and presentation of research-driven statistical methods, contributing to peer-reviewed journals or corporate white papers.
Ensure ethical considerations in statistical practices, addressing biases, ensuring transparency, and maintaining the integrity of research.

technical_competencies.name: Artificial Intelligence Techniques
technical_competencies.description: The Artificial Intelligence Techniques competency encompasses the knowledge and skills required to develop, deploy, and manage AI-driven solutions, including machine learning algorithms, deep learning models, natural language processing (NLP), and generative AI systems. It covers the full AI pipeline from data preparation and model development to ethical considerations and model deployment.
technical_competencies.why_this_competency_matters: As AI continues to revolutionize industries, the ability to apply AI techniques effectively is crucial for data science professionals and AI experts. Mastering AI enables organizations to harness the power of automation, predictive modeling, and data-driven decision-making. This competency empowers teams to solve complex problems, optimize processes, and create innovative AI-powered products, ensuring the organization stays competitive in a rapidly evolving technological landscape. Moreover, responsible AI practices ensure that the solutions are ethical, fair, and transparent, which is essential for building trust and meeting regulatory requirements.

Foundational: Apply basic machine learning algorithms, including supervised and unsupervised techniques.
Define core AI concepts, such as machine learning, deep learning, large language models, and vision-language models.
Use open-source libraries to build basic models.
Perform effective prompt engineering.
Evaluate the quality of LLM's.
Intermediate: Apply deep learning modeling approaches to solve problems.
Apply AI techniques to real-world business problems, demonstrating the ability to develop AI-powered solutions and research.
Fine-tune models and evaluate performance using appropriate metrics (e.g., accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score).
Fine-tune generative AI processes and LLMs.
Recognize the ethical implications of AI, focusing on fairness, bias reduction, and trust in AI design.
Identify AI/data science trends and tools.
Use prompt engineering to guide AI agents in performing structured data tasks.
Use complex prompting and quality assurance techniques.
Generate augmented retrieval and tooling.
Implement modular AI workflows using tools like LangGraph or orchestrator-worker patterns.
Integrate AI agents into existing pipelines (e.g., for NLP, geospatial, or statistical modelling tasks).
Use AI-generated outputs responsibly by applying validation techniques and human-in-the-loop review.
Monitor agent performance using defined metrics (e.g., accuracy, latency, reproducibility).
Advanced: Apply complex AI methodologies (e.g., convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs)) to complex problems (e.g., those involving multiple types of data, high ethical risks, or large impacts from errors).
Design and build production-ready AI solutions, including large language models (LLMs) and generative AI systems.
Apply and fine-tune tree-based algorithms such as decision trees, logistic regression, or clustering techniques.
Develop and deploy machine learning pipelines for production.
Implement deployment strategies for AI systems, including monitoring and maintaining performance post-deployment.
Stay up to date with emerging AI techniques and assess their applicability to business problems.
Identify AI/data science trends and tools, and their potential impacts.
Identify all challenges (e.g., hallucination, bias, replication, etc.) and benefits of AI.
Monitor automated decisions post-implementation for unintended outcomes.
Monitor AI systems for health, bias, and data drift.
Architect and deploy multi-agent systems capable of reasoning, planning, and acting autonomously.
Design and implement data workflows that combine prompt chaining, routing, and evaluator-optimizer loops.
Lead: Develop and implement AI strategies within an organization, ensuring alignment of AI initiatives with business goals.
Champion responsible and explainable AI practices, ensuring transparency and accountability in AI systems.
Identify opportunities to monetize AI solutions, creating product-led solutions to build lasting value.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to steer AI systems and integrate AI solutions across various business functions.
Support the establishment of standards and frameworks for the responsible use of data science and artificial intelligence within the government.
Assess and guide the evaluation of data-related capabilities, limitations, risks, trends, and provide strategic recommendations for the application of AI techniques within a business context.
Set/enforce AI deployment processes from ingestion to maintenance.

technical_competencies.name: Scientific Research Methods
technical_competencies.description: This competency encompasses the systematic application of scientific principles and methodologies to investigate data-driven questions. It involves formulating hypotheses, designing experiments, collecting and analyzing data, and interpreting results to derive meaningful conclusions.
technical_competencies.why_this_competency_matters: In the realm of data science, the ability to apply rigorous scientific methods ensures that analyses are valid, reliable, and reproducible. This competency is crucial for developing models and insights that stand up to scrutiny and contribute to evidence-based decision-making.

Foundational: Grasp basic concepts of the scientific method, including hypothesis formulation and experimental design.
Conduct literature reviews to answer research questions.
Interpret simple research findings and conclusions within the context.
Familiarity with data collection techniques and tools, such as surveys, focused groups (e.g. mixed methods, qualitative and/or quantitative research methods).
Intermediate: Design and implement experiments with appropriate controls and variables (e.g. define research problem and identify methodology to answer); ensure data collection directly tied to hypotheses/questions.
Apply statistical methods to analyze experimental data and test hypotheses including metrics such as confidence intervals, sensitivity, specificity, etc.
Understand and apply ethical standards in research, including data privacy and consent.
Advanced: Develop and manage complex studies, including applying novel methods to new areas as well as combining and interpreting findings across research experiments.
Understand the pros and cons of different experiment designs and statistical methods and when one is more appropriate.
Conduct methodological reviews and referee research reports to ensure robustness in methods used and validity of findings.
Ensure research findings are reproducible and validate models across different datasets.
Lead: Spearhead cross-functional research teams and oversee multiple research projects.
Align research initiatives with organizational goals and strategy.
Drive innovation in research methods and contribute to scholarly publications.
Review research to assess business impacts, risks, or sensitivities.

technical_competencies.name: Code Management
technical_competencies.description: Code Management involves the systematic use of tools, practices, and methodologies to organize, version, document, and maintain source code in data science and artificial intelligence (AI) projects. It includes version control, modular code organization, documentation standards, and collaborative workflows to ensure code is reproducible, scalable, and maintainable.
technical_competencies.why_this_competency_matters: Code Management is critical in data science and AI because these fields often involve complex, iterative workflows with multiple contributors. Effective code management ensures that code is reusable, reproducible, and maintainable, reducing errors and technical debt. It facilitates collaboration across teams, supports scalable deployment of models, and ensures compliance with organizational and regulatory standards. Poor code management can Lead to inefficiencies, loss of intellectual property, or project failures due to untraceable changes or lack of documentation.

Foundational: Recall the purpose of version control systems (e.g., Git) and their role in collaborative coding.
Explain the need for basic code documentation and consistent file structures in projects that involve programming.
Execute basic version control commands (e.g., git commit, git push) to manage code changes.
Intermediate: Implement branching and merging strategies in Git to manage collaborative codebases.
Organize repository and packaging the code to ensure clean code and documentation management practices at the end of project development.
Document functions and scripts using standardized formats (e.g., Python docstrings) to ensure reproducibility.
Review and test AI-assisted code to ensure validity, relevance and adherence to GoC standards.
Advanced: Evaluate version control workflows to identify inefficiencies in large-scale coding projects involving multiple contributors.
Organize repository and packaging the code to ensure clean code and documentation management practices at the end of project development.
Develop and enforce coding standards and tests (e.g., PEP 8) for code reviews to maintain high-quality, reproducible code.
Mentor and coach to improve team proficiency in code management practices and ensure adherence to standards.
Apply and promote responsible AI practices in code development and maintenance.
Lead: Establish organizational code management practices to ensure departmental policies are met (such as retention policies and information management requirements).
Monitor and oversee access and permissions to codebases.
Lead governance and ethical oversight of AI use in code management across projects or teams.

technical_competencies.name: Technical Communication
technical_competencies.description: Technical communication is the ability to effectively convey complex data and analytical insights to diverse audiences, ensuring clarity, accuracy, and relevance. This competency encompasses presenting information using appropriate visual and narrative techniques, adapting messaging to suit stakeholder needs, and linking data findings to organizational objectives. Strong technical communicators make data accessible and actionable, bridging the gap between technical analysis and business decision-making. Mastery of this skill empowers teams to drive informed strategies and foster collaboration across the organization.
technical_competencies.why_this_competency_matters: Communicating statistical and data science methods and storytelling through data transforms analysis into compelling narratives that drive action. Data Science and AI practitioners must craft clear, persuasive data stories aligned with stakeholder needs and strategic objectives. Capacity to communicate technical and non-technical information to clients and other audiences.

Foundational: Present basic data analysis results in clear, simple terms using basic charts and graphs (e.g., bar charts, line plots), ensuring key insights are understandable to technical and non-technical audiences.
Summarize the findings of simple analyses (e.g., descriptive statistics or basic trends) in a straightforward manner. Focus on clarity and conciseness.
Use basic visual tools (e.g., Excel charts, basic Python/R plotting) to represent data in ways that make trends and relationships easy to understand.
Use appropriate data/AI terms and concepts when communicating.
Cite sources of information/AI-generated content in visuals.
Intermediate: Organize data insights into a clear, logical structure, ensuring the narrative flow is easy to follow and the key insights are highlighted.
Create complex visualizations (e.g., heatmaps, scatter plots, time series plots) to demonstrate trends, correlations, or distributions, providing more detailed insights for specific audiences.
Adapt communication approach for different stakeholders (e.g., technical team vs. business Leaders), ensuring that the level of complexity is appropriate for the audience.
Develop data-driven narratives that directly link findings to business objectives, demonstrating how the insights impact strategy and decision-making.
Communicate risks of AI-generated content (e.g., copyright, bias, etc.).
Advanced: Apply in-depth knowledge of related policies, stakeholders and operational procedures in their explanation of complex topics to increase relatability, comprehension and overall understanding.
Integrate multiple data sources and variables into cohesive, actionable visuals and stories that explain complex patterns and trends and highlight key insights.
Lead: Guide teams in developing and presenting data-driven communication strategies, to influence organizational decision-making at the highest levels.
Mentor and Lead teams in crafting high-level data stories, ensuring that data insights align with broader business goals and are effectively communicated across departments.
Develop and oversee the design of organizational frameworks for communicating complex data findings and ensuring consistency and clarity across the organization.
Guide discussions to engage key business stakeholders with data insights, ensuring that they understand and act on the findings in a way that aligns with business strategy.

technical_competencies.name: Project Management
technical_competencies.description: Project Management in the context of data science involves planning, organizing, and overseeing data-driven projects from initiation to completion. It includes managing resources, timelines, and deliverables while ensuring that project goals align with business objectives. It also involves risk management, stakeholder communication, and iterative problem-solving throughout the project lifecycle.
technical_competencies.why_this_competency_matters: Project management is a crucial competency in ensuring that data science projects are delivered on time, within scope, and meet business needs. Effective project management ensures that teams are aligned, resources are optimally used, and that potential risks and obstacles are addressed proactively. In a data science context, the ability to manage complex, data-driven projects allows organizations to make informed decisions, achieve key objectives, and optimize business processes based on insights from data.

Foundational: Assist in planning project tasks and timelines, and ensure milestones are met under direct supervision.
Help allocate resources (time, people, tools) for simple tasks or project phases.
Understand and follow project timelines and task lists.
Identify simple project risks, such as timeline delays or resource shortages, and raise awareness with the team.
Contribute to maintaining project documentation (e.g., status reports, project timelines) and keep records updated.
Intermediate: Independently manage smaller, less complex tasks within a project, ensuring deadlines and deliverables are met.
Monitor the progress of data science projects, ensuring the team stays on track, and adjust when necessary (e.g., reallocating resources or extending deadlines).
Identify and mitigate moderate risks in data science projects, including technical issues, resource shortages, or data availability concerns.
Provide regular updates to stakeholders on the status of the project, ensuring clear communication of timelines, issues, and changes.
Engage with users to collect feedback/data during idea/solution implementation.
Engage in evidence-building activities throughout the project cycle.
Flag AI/data governance issues.
Adjust work based on continuous user feedback.
Register new AI solutions/projects with appropriate stakeholders.
Advanced: Head the planning and structuring of complex data science projects, setting clear goals, objectives, and deliverables.
Manage project resources effectively, including personnel, budget, and tools, ensuring optimal allocation for project success.
Proactively identify and manage Advanced project risks (e.g., scope creep, major technical challenges), implementing solutions to mitigate potential issues.
Lead coordination between cross-functional teams (data scientists, engineers, business stakeholders) to ensure alignment of project goals and seamless execution.
Prioritize evidence-based knowledge/data over conjecture (e.g., in data storytelling).
Promote self-serve access by design.
Work in a multidisciplinary team to inform problem framing with data.
Consider data use at the outset of a project.
Set analysis goals collaboratively with stakeholders.
Obtain stakeholder agreement on assessment criteria before implementation.
Prototype solutions for demonstration in customer environments.
Test solutions with diverse data for inclusiveness by design.
Ensure that projects are accessible by design.
Lead: Oversee and guide large-scale data science projects, ensuring alignment with organizational strategy and business objectives.
Manage and optimize the execution of multiple complex projects, ensuring efficient resource allocation, and driving continuous improvements in processes.
Manage stakeholder relationships and expectations, ensuring clear communication throughout the project lifecycle.
Drive engagement and alignment on strategic decisions.
Mentor junior team members, providing Leadership in project management best practices.
Guide teams in tackling complex challenges and delivering results.
Identify opportunities to innovate and improve project management practices, introducing new methodologies and tools to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of data science projects.
Collaborate with relevant specialists (e.g., data/AI/legal/privacy/IM/IT experts).
Own end-to-end pipelines considering full data lifecycle.
Identify and remove roadblocks to efficient data/AI work (e.g., issues relating to infrastructure, tools, training gaps, etc.).

technical_competencies.name: Business Acumen
technical_competencies.description: Business acumen in data science refers to the ability to understand and apply knowledge of business operations, strategy, and decision-making processes. It involves identifying business needs, aligning data-driven insights with organizational goals, and making decisions that drive organizational success.
technical_competencies.why_this_competency_matters: Business acumen is crucial for ensuring that data science initiatives are aligned with the broader goals of the organization. Data science doesn't exist in a vacuum; its results must be actionable, valuable, and relevant to business stakeholders. Data professionals who possess business acumen can bridge the gap between data insights and strategic decisions, ensuring that their work drives measurable impact, fosters innovation, and supports long-term business growth.

Foundational: Demonstrate basic understanding of key business functions, such as marketing, finance, and operations, and how they relate to data science projects.
Recognize business problems and basic opportunities where data analysis can contribute to business goals.
Understand key financial metrics (e.g., revenue, profit margins, cost structures) and how they impact business decisions.
Present data findings in simple terms, ensuring they are relevant and understandable for business stakeholders.
Recognize various data types and value as an organizational asset.
Intermediate: Collaborate with business teams to identify key business objectives and tailor data science projects to align with those objectives.
Assess the potential impact of data science solutions on business performance and communicate how the findings can influence business decisions.
Conduct market research or competitive analysis to understand industry trends and incorporate relevant external data into business decisions.
Work with cross-functional teams (e.g., marketing, finance, product) to ensure data projects are aligned with business priorities.
Tie visualizations explicitly to business rationale and intended use.
Advanced: Lead efforts to translate data insights into actionable strategies that drive business growth and optimize business processes.
Conduct Advanced market analysis and competitive intelligence to inform business decisions and strategy.
Apply data science techniques to identify inefficiencies in business operations and recommend process improvements.
Identify potential risks to business performance and use data analysis to evaluate and mitigate those risks.
Apply principles of business analysis to government operations and process for access and interoperability.
Lead: Head the creation of data-driven business models that optimize profitability, revenue generation, or customer engagement. Ensure alignment with long-term business strategy.
Guide senior Leadership on strategic decisions based on data insights, providing recommendations that align with both short- and long-term business goals.
Champion the integration of data-driven decision-making across all business functions, promoting a culture of data-driven Leadership.
Manage cross-functional teams to ensure data-driven projects meet organizational goals and generate measurable business value.
Head innovation initiatives that leverage data science to transform business processes, create new revenue streams, or disrupt the market.
Help others translate organizational needs/mandate into data/AI requirements for projects.
Apply governance in specific operational business contexts (e.g., obtaining policy guideline approval).
Define and implement strategies for advancing organizational AI talent, systems, and infrastructure.
